headings.title: Solar energy property right and condemnation prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Covers recognition of solar energy utilization as a property right and prohibition against using eminent domain to acquire solar property rights.

headings.title: Written solar easements, recording rules, and negative easement status
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirements for writing, angles, and recording of solar easements, and characterization as negative easements not acquirable by prescription.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: solar energy property right with eminent domain bar and written/recorded negative solar easement requirements.

headings.title: Short title
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory designation as the Private Landowner Protection Act.

headings.title: Definitions for conservation easements
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory definitions for conservation easement, holder, and third-party right of enforcement.

headings.title: Creation, acceptance, unlimited duration, and existing interests
headings.reviewNote: Covers creation, conveyance, recording, mandatory acceptance, unlimited duration, and protection of pre-existing property interests.

headings.title: Standing to bring judicial action and court modification power
headings.reviewNote: Covers standing of owners, holders, and third-party enforcers, and court authority to modify or terminate conservation easements in equity.

headings.title: Validity notwithstanding common-law impediments
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory validity of conservation easements despite lack of appurtenance, traditional character, touching/concerning, or privity.

headings.title: Public utility condemnation and easement rights preserved
headings.reviewNote: Covers preservation of public utility and municipal utility authority to acquire utility easements across conservation easements.

headings.title: Applicability to prospective and retroactive interests
headings.reviewNote: Covers application to interests created after effective date, retroactive application where constitutional, and non-impairment of prior terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections against archived text (noting "This act" footnote and section 640.099 nonseverability cross-reference): Private Landowner Protection Act conservation easements, standing, common-law validity, utility rights, and retroactive scope.

headings.title: Manufactured home and permanent affixation defined
headings.reviewNote: Covers definition of manufactured home, real property status under bankruptcy law, and standards for permanent foundation and utility affixation.

headings.title: Conditions for conveyance or encumbrance as real estate
headings.reviewNote: Covers four statutory conditions for conveying or encumbering manufactured homes as real estate, including affixation and certified filings.

headings.title: Required contents and attachments of affidavit of affixation
headings.reviewNote: Covers required contents of affidavit of affixation including home details, ownership, lease terms, legal description, and title status.

headings.title: Prior security interests and liens unimpaired
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that permanent affixation and recording an affidavit of affixation do not impair existing security interests or liens.

headings.title: Recorder delivery of certified copy and revenue filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires recorder of deeds to deliver a certified copy of the recorded affidavit of affixation and attachments to the delivering party, and requires the designated person to file it with the director of revenue under subsection 2(4).

headings.title: Events required for manufactured home to be deemed real estate
headings.reviewNote: Lists four required events before a manufactured home is deemed real estate: permanent affixation, recorded affidavit of affixation, delivery of certified copy to director of revenue, and compliance with section 700.111(1)–(3).

headings.title: Legal effect as real estate and real estate lien attachment
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that upon satisfying subsection 6 the home is governed by real estate laws, real estate mortgages/liens attach from recording as if site-built, and title transfers by real estate conveyance together with the land.

headings.title: Affidavit ineffective without statutory compliance
headings.reviewNote: Covers provision that affidavits of affixation are not effective to convey or alter chattel character without meeting statutory requirements.

headings.title: Pre-existing property rights unimpaired
headings.reviewNote: Covers non-impairment of property rights or interests in manufactured homes existing prior to August 28, 2010.

headings.title: Severance affidavit and conversion back to personal property
headings.reviewNote: Requires recording an acknowledged affidavit of severance upon detachment from real estate, including home details, affixation recording reference, title/lien knowledge statement, attorney or title-agent free-and-clear declaration, and filing designee.

headings.title: Recorder delivery of severance affidavit and revenue filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires recorder of deeds to deliver a certified copy of the affidavit of severance to the delivering party, and requires the designated person to deliver it and required documents to the director of revenue.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 11 subsections against archived text (effective 3-01-11); fixed hallucinated "notice to assessor" in subsections 5 and 11 (actually director of revenue filing) and corrected reviewNotes in subsections 6, 7, and 10.

headings.title: Conveyance to self and others creating joint estate
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any real estate owner to convey property to himself or themselves and others to create a joint tenancy, tenancy by the entireties, tenancy in common, or tenancy in partnership with the same effect as a conveyance from a stranger.

headings.title: Conveyance by co-owners to one or more of themselves
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes two or more real estate owners to convey property to one, more than one, or all of themselves to create separate ownership or co-tenancy with the same effect as a conveyance from a stranger.

headings.title: Inclusion of married persons as grantors or grantees
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that any "person" or "persons" referenced in section 442.025 may be married persons or persons married to each other.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced all 3 completely hallucinated draft headings (which erroneously described marital trusts) with source-bound headings for conveyances to self and others creating joint estates; noted section 513.475 cross-reference and 1954/1960/1961 case annotations.

headings.title: Conservator authority to join in entireties property disposition
headings.reviewNote: Grants conservators of minor (under 18) or chapter 475 disabled spouses full power, acting with the other spouse or conservator and subject to subsections 2 and 3, to sell, encumber, lease, partition, or convert entireties property.

headings.title: Probate division supervision and equitable approval standard
headings.reviewNote: Covers probate court approval, supervision, equity finding for protectees, chapter 475 procedures, and taxation of costs.

headings.title: Guardian ad litem appointment when spouse serves as conservator
headings.reviewNote: Covers appointment of guardian ad litem to represent protectee in negotiations when the other spouse serves as conservator.

headings.title: Exemption for married minors authorized to convey
headings.reviewNote: Covers non-applicability of conservatorship disposition rules to married individuals under eighteen legally authorized to convey in person.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text (effective 7-01-97); updated subsection 1 reviewNote to include minor spouses under 18 alongside disabled spouses.

headings.title: Veteran execution of instruments under Servicemen's Readjustment Act
headings.reviewNote: Covers authority of Missouri resident veterans to execute deeds of trust, mortgages, or powers of attorney under federal readjustment law.

headings.title: Veteran authority to contract and borrow for home or business property
headings.reviewNote: Covers veteran power to contract or borrow funds to purchase or construct homes, farm structures, and business properties.

headings.title: Veteran borrowing for home repairs, improvements, or delinquent taxes
headings.reviewNote: Covers authority of veterans to borrow money for residential repairs, alterations, improvements, or delinquent tax and assessment payments.

headings.title: Veteran borrowing for agricultural operations or business pursuits
headings.reviewNote: Covers authority to borrow for farm equipment, livestock, land, supplies, business machinery, or gainful occupation pursuits.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text: Missouri resident veteran authority to execute instruments, contract, and borrow under the Servicemen's Readjustment Act of 1944.

headings.title: Minor veteran and spouse contract rights under Servicemen's Readjustment Act
headings.reviewNote: Covers equal rights and liabilities for minor veterans and minor spouses entering guaranteed loans and contracts as if over twenty-one.

headings.title: Prohibition against repudiation upon reaching majority
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against veterans aged eighteen to twenty-one repudiating written loan obligations upon attaining age twenty-one.

headings.title: Ratification of instruments executed prior to effective date
headings.reviewNote: Validates, ratifies, and confirms Servicemen's Readjustment Act loan instruments executed by veterans aged 18 to 21 prior to the effective date of sections 442.100 to 442.120 (source footnote: July 24, 1945).

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text including July 24, 1945 effective-date footnote in subsection 3: removal of minority disability for eligible veterans and spouses aged 18 to 21, non-repudiation, and prior-instrument ratification.

headings.title: Subscription, acknowledgment, and certification of conveyances
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that deeds and conveyances of land be subscribed by granting parties or lawful agents and acknowledged or proved.

headings.title: Mandatory disclosure of marital status of natural parties
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that all written real estate conveyance instruments state whether natural granting or executing parties are married or unmarried.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text (noting Revisor's Note that H.B. 1606 was held unconstitutional in Byrd v. State while identical H.B. 1662 remains in effect, plus 2002 Beck v. Beck annotation).

headings.title: Preparer identification and license number on new property descriptions
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that new property descriptions created upon subdivision include the preparer's name and professional license number.

headings.title: Recording prohibition absent required preparer identification
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against submitting conveyance instruments for recording if the subdivided property description lacks preparer information.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: preparer name and license number required on new subdivided property descriptions and recording prohibition absent that information.

headings.title: Execution of conveyances in foreign language
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorization for deeds, mortgages, and acknowledgments executed in foreign countries to be made in the language of such country.

headings.title: Sworn English translation required for recording and evidence
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement of sworn English translation by recorder of land titles for foreign-language deeds to be recorded and received in evidence.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: foreign-language execution of conveyances in foreign countries and sworn English translation requirement for recording and evidence.

headings.title: Methods of personal appearance for statutory acknowledgments
headings.reviewNote: Covers personal appearance methods by physical presence or authorized remote communication technology under chapter 486.

headings.title: Designation of appearance method in certificate of acknowledgment
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that acknowledging officer designate physical or communication technology appearance on the statutory certificate.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: physical or chapter 486 communication-technology personal appearance for acknowledgments and mandatory certificate designation.

headings.title: Authority of real estate officers to take proof of any writing
headings.reviewNote: Covers extension of power to officers authorized to acknowledge real estate conveyances to take proof or acknowledgment of any written instrument.

headings.title: Standard certificate of proof or acknowledgment applicable
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that certificates of proof or acknowledgment conform to real estate conveyance certificate standards.

headings.title: Validation of prior non-real estate acknowledgments without rerecording
headings.reviewNote: Covers retrospective validation of prior acknowledgments of non-real estate instruments without need for rerecording.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text: real-estate officer authority to acknowledge any written instrument, standard certificate format, and curative validation without rerecording.

headings.title: Armed forces commissioned officer authority to take acknowledgments
headings.reviewNote: Covers authority of commissioned military officers to take acknowledgments of service members and spouses with notary public effect.

headings.title: Officer certification, security omissions, and prima facie evidence
headings.reviewNote: Covers required officer certification elements, security exceptions for omitting details, and officer grade as prima facie authority.

headings.title: Statutory military acknowledgment form
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory form of acknowledgment satisfying all legal requirements for military acknowledgments.

headings.title: Validation of prior military acknowledgments without rerecording
headings.reviewNote: Covers validation of prior nonconforming military acknowledgments conforming to current section standards without rerecording.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections (including embedded statutory form, effective 6-12-91) against archived text: commissioned military officer acknowledgment authority, certification/security omissions, form, and curative validation.

headings.title: Contents of certificate and forms for individuals, attorneys, and entities
headings.reviewNote: Covers required knowledge/witness recitals and statutory acknowledgment forms for individuals, attorneys-in-fact, and corporations.

headings.title: Acknowledgment form when corporation lacks corporate seal
headings.reviewNote: Covers modification of corporate acknowledgment form when the corporation or association does not maintain a corporate seal.

headings.title: Officer signature and title required on all certificates
headings.reviewNote: Covers mandatory addition of signature and official title of the acknowledging officer to all certificates of acknowledgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections (including embedded natural-person, attorney, and corporate forms) against archived text: certificate contents, no-seal corporate modification, and officer signature/title.

headings.title: Discriminatory restrictive covenants void and unenforceable
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that restrictive covenant recitals relating to race, color, religion, or national origin are void, unenforceable, and ignored.

headings.title: Immunity for pre-1948 recorded restrictive covenants
headings.reviewNote: Covers immunity protecting property owners and agents from liability arising from mere existence of pre-May 3, 1948 recorded restrictive covenants.

headings.title: Prohibition on specific reference in deeds and recorder refusal
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition on referencing discriminatory covenants in deeds after August 28, 2022, recorder rejection, and validity of mistaken transfers.

headings.title: Certificate of release of prohibited covenants and statutory form
headings.reviewNote: Covers owner authority to record certificate releasing prohibited covenants and provides statutory release form.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections (including embedded release form) against archived text: void discriminatory covenants, pre-May 3, 1948 immunity, post-August 28, 2022 deed reference bar and recorder refusal, and owner release certificate.

headings.title: Definitions for homeowners' associations, signs, and solar panels
headings.reviewNote: Defines "homeowners' association" (excluding condominium associations under section 448.1-103(3) and residential cooperatives), "political signs", and "solar panel or solar collector".

headings.title: Political signs, reasonable association rules, and removal notice
headings.reviewNote: Bars deed restrictions or covenants prohibiting political signs, authorizes reasonable HOA time/size/place/number/manner rules, allows liability-free removal for specified violations, and requires 3 days written notice before removal or fining.

headings.title: Solar panel installation protections and reasonable placement rules
headings.reviewNote: Bars deed restrictions or covenants limiting or prohibiting rooftop solar panels/collectors, allows reasonable HOA placement rules that do not impair functioning or adversely affect cost or efficiency, and limits scope to owner-controlled rooftops.

headings.title: Sale signs, reasonable association rules, and removal notice
headings.reviewNote: Bars deed restrictions or covenants prohibiting sale signs on property or nearby street corners, authorizes reasonable HOA rules, allows liability-free removal for specified violations, and requires 3 business days written notice before removal or fining.

headings.title: Ownership or pasturing of up to six chickens
headings.reviewNote: Bars deed restrictions or covenants prohibiting ownership or pasturing of up to six chickens (and a single coop) on lots of 0.2 acres or larger, while allowing reasonable HOA rules including rooster prohibitions.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced all 5 shifted/hallucinated draft headings with source-bound headings matching definitions, political signs, solar panels, sale signs, and chickens; noted 2026 Eikmeier v. Granite Springs HOA case annotation.

headings.title: Validity of non-violating limitations and dispositive scheme test
headings.reviewNote: Preserves validity of non-violating limitations or provisions in an instrument containing a limitation violating the rule against perpetuities unless the violating provision is manifestly essential to the dispositive scheme, resolving doubts toward validity.

headings.title: Judicial reformation of violating limitations on timely petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires a court of competent jurisdiction, on timely petition by any party in interest with process served on all parties, to reform a violating limitation if reformation more closely approximates the creator's primary purpose than total invalidity.

headings.title: Exclusion of perpetuities periods running before November 1
headings.reviewNote: Excludes from section 442.555 any limitation or provision for which the rule against perpetuities period began to run prior to November 1 of the year the section became effective.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced all 3 shifted/hallucinated draft headings with source-bound headings matching severability of non-violating limitations, judicial reformation on timely petition, and November 1 effective-date exclusion.

headings.title: Definitions for transfer fee covenants
headings.reviewNote: Defines "transfer", "transfer fee" (with six exclusions including purchase consideration, broker commissions, lender fees, lease payments, option/first-refusal payments, and government charges), and "transfer fee covenant".

headings.title: Post-September 2008 transfer fee covenants and liens void
headings.reviewNote: Declares transfer fee covenants recorded on or after September 1, 2008 not to run with title and unenforceable against subsequent owners, purchasers, or mortgagees, and voids any lien securing such fees.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced both completely hallucinated draft headings (which erroneously described trust rule against perpetuities) with source-bound headings for transfer fee covenant definitions and post-September 1, 2008 invalidity.

headings.title: Prohibition on foreign ownership of agricultural land exceeding one percent
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory restriction barring foreign acquisition of agricultural land if aggregate foreign ownership exceeds one percent of total state farmland.

headings.title: Continuing violation during unlawful holding and lien preservation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an alien or foreign business acquiring agricultural land in violation of sections 442.560 to 442.592 remains in violation while holding any interest, without divesting or invalidating any security interest.

headings.title: Department of agriculture review of proposed foreign acquisitions
headings.reviewNote: Requires submission of proposed agricultural land acquisitions (subject to subsection 1) to the department of agriculture to determine compliance with the one-percent cap and directs rulemaking for submissions and approvals.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires chapter 536 and section 536.028 compliance for rules under section 442.571 and includes a nonseverability clause invalidating post-August 28, 2014 rulemaking if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsection 1 and replaced hallucinated/shifted draft headings in subsections 2, 3, and 4 (continuing violation, department review, chapter 536 rulemaking/nonseverability); noted 1995 and 1997 Von Kerssenbrock-Praschma annotations.

headings.title: Director report of unlawful foreign land acquisitions to attorney general
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director of agriculture to report to the attorney general if an alien, foreign business, or fiduciary acquired agricultural land in violation of sections 442.560 to 442.592 or ceased nonagricultural use under section 442.591.

headings.title: Attorney general circuit court enforcement action and venue
headings.reviewNote: Requires the attorney general to institute a circuit court enforcement action in Cole County or any county where the subject agricultural land is located.

headings.title: Lis pendens, two-year divestiture order, and public sale
headings.reviewNote: Requires lis pendens filing, court declaration and 2-year divestiture order running with title (referencing Missouri Constitution Art. XI § 5 for incorporated foreign businesses; source footnote notes repeal in 1988), and foreclosure-style public sale upon noncompliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced all 3 shifted/hallucinated draft headings with source-bound headings for director reporting, attorney general circuit court action, and lis pendens/divestiture/public sale; noted 10-11-13 veto override and 1988 repeal of referenced Art. XI § 5.

headings.title: Foreign person defined
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory definition of foreign person including nonresident aliens, foreign entities, foreign-controlled domestic entities, and foreign governments.

headings.title: Reporting requirements for pre-existing foreign agricultural holdings
headings.reviewNote: Covers sixty-day reporting mandate for foreign persons holding agricultural land interests on September 28, 1979, and mineral extraction exemptions.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking authority under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that rules promulgated under sections 442.560 to 442.591 comply with section 536.024 rulemaking provisions.

headings.title: Thirty-day reporting requirement for foreign agricultural land transfers
headings.reviewNote: Covers thirty-day reporting obligation to director of agriculture following any acquisition or transfer of agricultural land interests by foreign persons.

headings.title: Promulgation of reporting forms and content regulations
headings.reviewNote: Covers director of agriculture authority to adopt rules regarding report forms, filing procedures, and information distribution.

headings.title: Director analysis of family farm impacts and legislative reporting
headings.reviewNote: Covers director duty to analyze agricultural land holdings data, determine family farm and community impacts, and report findings to the legislature.

headings.title: Civil penalty up to twenty-five percent and attorney general enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Covers civil liability up to twenty-five percent of fair market value for failure to report and attorney general civil recovery action in circuit court.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections against archived text: foreign person definition, pre-1979 and 30-day transfer reporting (with mineral extraction exemptions), section 536.024 rulemaking, director analysis/reports, and up-to-25% civil penalty.

headings.title: Psychological impacts not material facts requiring real estate disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that proximity to or characterization as psychologically impacted property is not a material fact requiring disclosure in sales.

headings.title: Psychologically impacted real property defined
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory definition including occupant HIV infection, non-transmissible medical conditions, felony, homicide, or suicide occurrences.

headings.title: Immunity for real estate brokers and agents
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against causes of action against real estate agents or brokers for failing to disclose psychologically impacted property.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text: non-materiality of psychologically impacted real property, statutory definition, and broker/agent immunity.

headings.title: Mandatory written disclosure of prior methamphetamine production
headings.reviewNote: Covers seller duty to disclose prior methamphetamine production on premises in writing based on seller's actual knowledge.

headings.title: Mandatory written disclosure of resident methamphetamine convictions
headings.reviewNote: Requires written disclosure if premises served as residence, storage site, or lab for specified methamphetamine convictions (if seller knew or should have known); source footnotes note 2014 transfers of §§ 195.420/195.233 and repeal of § 195.246 effective 1-01-17.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text; noted 2014 transfer/repeal footnotes (effective 1-01-17) for sections 195.420, 195.233, and 195.246 in subsection 2.

headings.title: Short title
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory designation as the Missouri Residential Sale Leaseback Protection Act.

headings.title: Definitions for residential sale leasebacks
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory definitions for buyer, residential real estate, sale leaseback, and seller.

headings.title: Required boldface warning disclosure and fourteen-day delivery rule
headings.reviewNote: Covers mandatory single-page boldface warning disclosure provided fourteen days prior to execution and signed copies within five days.

headings.title: Thirty-day title transfer moratorium following agreement execution
headings.reviewNote: Covers thirty-day moratorium prohibiting delivery, recording, or transfer of real estate title following execution of sale leaseback agreements.

headings.title: Civil penalties, attorney general enforcement, and private rights of action
headings.reviewNote: Covers $10,000 civil penalty, attorney general enforcement powers, and private actions for actual and statutory damages and attorney fees.

headings.title: Nonwaivability and invalidation of post-2026 modification agreements
headings.reviewNote: Covers nonwaiver provision declaring any agreement executed after August 28, 2026, modifying or waiving statutory protections void ab initio.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections (including embedded boldface disclosure form, L. 2026 H.B. 2636 merged with S.B. 834 & S.B. 973) against archived text: Missouri Residential Sale Leaseback Protection Act.
